title: Go-live readiness
intro: What must be true before Amplify goes public at UK Parliament Week, what has been tested and how, what is still open and who must act, and the self-routines that keep it right once it is live. Must items block the public launch; Should and Could items do not, but are tracked.

gates.item: Every screen says whether its content is sourced, a planning model, a sample, generated or editorial
Claims checked against review findings: no other organisation inside UKYP's name, votes at 16 not stated as law, manifesto line credited
gates.note: Found and fixed during this review (D13 to D15).

gates.item: Every source has a provenance and a check date; overdue ones are flagged
Search-sourced facts (S) and leads (K) verified against primary sources where they matter most
gates.note: Most sources are search-sourced; the weekly run verifies them in turn. The live count is shown below.

gates.item: Helplines current and re-checked every 30 days; safeguarding linked from every Get involved screen
A named safeguarding lead and procedure before the ambassador programme or any research with under 18s starts
gates.note: Blocks those programmes, which stay as pilots; it does not block the information portal.

gates.item: WCAG 2.2 AA automated checks: axe-core in dark and light themes, keyboard, tooltips on focus, splash dialog
gates.note: The original design's own axe findings are a recorded baseline that may only shrink (O3).

gates.item: Testing with disabled people using their own technology, including d/Deaf BSL and ISL users
gates.note: Automated checks find perhaps a third of barriers; people find the rest.

gates.item: No sideways scrolling at 320 px (small phone), 768 px (tablet) and 1440 px, on every screen and the splash; the drawer scrolls on its own
Fast enough on a phone: the page is compiled in the browser by a bundled runtime, which is slow on low-end phones
gates.note: Measured every run against a budget. Compiling the page at build time would remove the runtime and make it much faster.

gates.item: Nothing reaches another host on load; no tracking; every library and font served by the portal
No email address anywhere; no personal data collected; contact by form only
Code scanning clean on every change
gates.note: One high finding (a case-sensitive check) was fixed as D10.

gates.item: A privacy notice for the research sign-up form
gates.note: Needed only when the private form exists.

gates.item: Every build verified, every check vaccinated, defects logged with a check
Weekly upkeep and weekly health checks scheduled, reporting to one place
Rollback: the previous version is kept and can be restored
gates.note: Git history and the artifact's own version history.

gates.item: Posters and cards print on their own; other screens are not yet print-tested
gates.note: The artwork viewer prints only the artwork. Whole screens have not been print-tested.

gates.item: The release candidate is reviewed and merged
Propriety: publishing under the owner's own name raises no issue with his employer
Decide how the portal is shared (the artifact is private until shared) and the address posters should point to
gates.note: Posters point to the public GitHub repository until then.

gates.item: Personas, journeys and stories tested with real users
gates.note: Launch is labelled as a prototype, with every model and sample marked.

gates.item: Welsh, Gaelic, Irish and sign-language versions of the most-used screens

routines.what: Every named change to the design must match exactly; vendored files match their pinned hashes; data parses
Repository, site and content rules, each proved by a deliberate break
Every screen at three widths, axe-core in both themes, tooltips, splash, phone speed
All checks plus the online link check, reported to one issue
Helplines first, then sources past review, new developments, issue triage, a pull request with a report
Freshness of every source and data file, with 30-day helpline and 90-day source reviews
Every defect gets a root cause, a fix, a check with a negative test and a register entry in one commit
The design's own axe findings may only shrink
Release log, registers, research bundle and service design are written from data, never by hand
Issues are checked for anything that identifies a person; the owner is told at once
CodeQL on Python, JavaScript and workflows
NEW and UPD flags in the drawer and on each screen come from the release log
Rounds, synthesis and You said, we did
Personas, stories and journeys updated from research findings
Testing with disabled people using their own technology
A check that the published portal loads, from outside the build
Notice when React, Babel, Leaflet or the icons have security releases
How the portal is archived or handed over if it stops being maintained
Gathers gates not passed, open items, requirements not done, sources and data files due a re-check and dates coming up into one public issue.
Thanks each new issue, labels it for triage, gives the helplines and flags anything that looks like an email address or phone number for a person to remove.
Fails the build if a release adds a term, tooltip, graph link or version without its glossary entry, or leaves the graph unparseable.
